summary: Draft cites 40 references and covers all nine claims, but 8 grep-verified vault notes are entirely unused. The load-bearing omissions are the N7 'roughen-the-GP-within-BO' near-miss (Ziomek/Osborne LB), the N6 'both-axes-varied-but-declined-ANOVA' near-miss (Moosbauer, which the step-8 corpus critic explicitly surfaced), and the N8 deep-RL determinism/reproducibility precursors (Machado, Islam) the task brief named. Report is 61.7KB, above the 45-55KB top-performer band, with a triply-repeated 'lead with D, hold C' recommendation.

findings.issue: The single closest 'roughen the GP within BO' near-miss in the vault is omitted, leaving N7's headline 'NONE FOUND, first at all, across the entire BO-and-kernel-methods literature' undefended against the paper a reviewer is most likely to raise. The coverage-gaps file (line 23-24) explicitly flagged this exact residual exposure: 'a NON-offline-MBO paper that ROUGHENS a smooth model.' Ziomek, Adachi & Osborne's Length-scale Balancing paper is the vault's answer to it (note is tagged locus-n7-roughening-beyond-offline-mbo) and the draft never engages it.
findings.evidence: Vault note bayesian-optimisation-with-unknown-hyperparameters-regret-bounds-logarithmically (Ziomek/Adachi/Osborne, arXiv:2410.10384, full body grepped): aggregates GP surrogates at multiple length-scales, 'intermittently adding smaller-length-scale (rougher) candidates while retaining longer-length-scale (smoother) ones' to minimize BO regret under unknown true smoothness. Note summary: 'stays entirely within the GP surrogate family (grep for neural network = 1 irrelevant hit) and never attributes a cross-surrogate-class performance gap to smoothness -- N7 stays NONE FOUND.' The draft currently supports N7's GP-side half only with ROOT [36] (offline-MBO length-scale-as-data-augmentation), not with this closer within-BO length-scale-varying analog.
findings.recommendation: In the N7 paragraph, alongside the ROOT sentence, add one sentence naming Ziomek/Adachi/Osborne (Length-scale Balancing) as the closest deliberate GP-smoothness manipulation in the BO literature and stating precisely why it does not own N7: it varies length-scale within a single surrogate family for regret bounds, never crosses surrogate classes and never causally attributes a class-gap to smoothness. This converts the 'first at all across BO/kernel methods' claim from an assertion into a defended rule-out.

findings.location: ## N6 - The Crossed Surrogate x Optimizer Factorial
findings.issue: The strongest 'both axes varied, variance decomposition deliberately declined' near-miss is missing from N6's rule-out table and prose. The step-8 corpus critic explicitly identified it as an N6 gap-fill find (corpus-critic-results.md, Gap 1). It is the single best evidence for N6's central argument that 'the gap is structural, not an artifact of incomplete search' -- a paper that HAD both surrogate-learner and search-strategy axes and consciously chose OFAT over fANOVA. Omitting it leaves N6 exposed to a reviewer who says 'Moosbauer already crossed surrogate and search strategy.'
findings.evidence: Vault note automated-benchmark-driven-design-and-explanation-of-hyperparameter-optimizers-i (Moosbauer et al., IEEE TEVC 2022, arXiv:2111.14756): varies HPO-internal surrogate learner (RF/KNN/TPE-density) AND sampling/search strategy, but 'explicitly discusses ANOVA/fANOVA... and deliberately does not use it,' choosing one-factor-at-a-time ablation and stating OFAT cannot detect interactions. corpus-critic-results.md Gap 1: 'Moosbauer et al. (IEEE TEVC 2022): discusses then rejects fANOVA for OFAT; varies surrogate + sampling separately, never a joint factorial.'
findings.recommendation: Add a row to the N6 rule-out table (Moosbauer: surrogate varied Yes / search varied Yes / variance decomposition No, OFAT by choice / offline MBO No) and one clause in the prose noting that the one paper closest to the two-axis design consciously declined the two-way variance decomposition -- the sharpest available evidence that the ANOVA-attribution gap is deliberate and structural, not a search artifact.

findings.location: ## N8 - Platform and Library-Version Dependence of Benchmark Results
findings.issue: Two grep-verified deep-RL reproducibility/determinism notes that the task brief named for N8 ('Nagarajan + Machado + Islam for N8') are entirely unused. The draft supports the 'environment variance same order as method signal' claim only with Nagarajan [19] (GPU nondeterminism) and Henderson [2] (codebase). Machado's ALE-determinism finding is directly on-point for N8's platform/determinism framing, and Islam is the earliest reproducibility-variance precursor -- both broaden the deep-RL evidence base that N8 leans on for its FOUND-in-deep-RL half.
findings.evidence: Vault notes: revisiting-the-arcade-learning-environment-evaluation-protocols-and-open-problem (Machado et al., JAIR 2018) names ALE emulator determinism enabling memorization-based score inflation and inconsistent protocol selection as confounds; and reproducibility-of-benchmarked-deep-reinforcement-learning-tasks-for-continuous (Islam et al., ICML 2017 Workshop) attributes divergent TRPO/DDPG results to environment stochasticity and hyperparameter under-reporting. grep of the draft confirms neither is cited (the only 'Islam' hit is Peter Henderson's co-author in ref [2]). Both were listed under N8 in coverage-gaps.md.
findings.recommendation: In the N8 paragraph, after the Nagarajan sentence, add one sentence citing Machado et al. (ALE emulator-determinism enabling score inflation) and Islam et al. (environment-stochasticity variance) as additional deep-RL precedents that the execution/protocol environment can move benchmark outcomes -- widening the 'FOUND in deep RL' base while preserving the offline-MBO/macOS-vs-Linux/same-order-ratio residual as NONE FOUND.

findings.location: ## N6 - The Crossed Surrogate x Optimizer Factorial
findings.issue: A third fANOVA-family near-miss is available but unused. The draft cites Hutter fANOVA [15] (one-way, one fixed search method) as the nearest variance-decomposition precedent; van Rijn & Hutter's KDD 2018 extension is a distinct, closer data point on how far the fANOVA lineage got without ever crossing model-class against search-strategy.
findings.evidence: Vault note hyperparameter-importance-across-datasets-kdd-2018-van-rijn-and-hutter-arxiv1710 (van Rijn & Hutter, KDD 2018): 'generalizes hyperparameter importance across many DATASETS for one algorithm at a time (SVM, then RF, then Adaboost, analyzed separately) -- never crosses model/algorithm class against optimizer/search-strategy class; does not even include model choice as a decomposed factor.'
findings.recommendation: Optionally append a half-sentence to the Hutter fANOVA discussion in N6 noting that even the fANOVA lineage's cross-dataset extension (van Rijn & Hutter 2018) analyzes one algorithm at a time and never decomposes model class against search strategy -- reinforcing that no descendant of fANOVA reaches the crossed two-axis decomposition.

findings.issue: The earliest paper in the IGNITE/ROOT smoothing lineage is omitted. N7 already cites IGNITE [18] and ROOT [36], but the vault contains a third same-group paper that independently confirms the lineage only ever reduces neural-net smoothness and never touches a GP -- adding independent weight to the 'one-directional, never crosses into GP territory' argument.
findings.evidence: Vault note boosting-offline-optimizers-with-surrogate-sensitivity-icml-2024-arxiv250304181 (Dao et al., ICML 2024): 'IGNITE's ICML 2024 precursor paper by the same author group: reduces (never increases) neural-network surrogate sensitivity, mentions a GP only as a bibliography citation with no GP experiment of its own -- second independent confirmation that this author lineage's smoothness work is one-directional and never crosses into GP.'
findings.recommendation: Optionally cite Dao et al. (ICML 2024, surrogate sensitivity) alongside IGNITE in N7's smoothness-as-regularization sentence, as a second independent instance of the lineage smoothing a network only, always downward, never a GP -- so the 'smooth-the-net half exists but never bidirectional' claim rests on two papers, not one.

findings.location: ## N5 - NTK / Spectral Bias and the Finite-Width Objection
findings.issue: The strongest NTK-literature-internal rebuttal to the finite-width objection is unused. N5 argues the width-fixes-it story is not fatal, but relies on L/R/W's architecture-size ablation [8] and Dai [32]. The direct empirical NTK-linearization follow-up (Lee/Xiao et al.) admits the linearized-regime agreement is architecture-dependent and an open question, and reports GPs still beat trained nets at all dataset sizes -- an admission from inside the NTK camp that width does not simply rescue finite nets, especially in offline MBO's small-data regime.
findings.evidence: Vault note wide-neural-networks-of-any-depth-evolve-as-linear-models-under-gradient-descent (Lee/Xiao/Schoenholz et al., NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1902.06720): agreement between finite nets and the NTK-linearized regime is 'highly architecture-dependent' and an 'open research question,' and 'GPs still outperform trained neural networks for both small and large dataset size, undercutting a pure width-fixes-it reading of N5.'
findings.recommendation: Optionally add one clause in N5 citing Lee/Xiao et al. (2019) that even the NTK-linearization literature reports finite-width/infinite-width agreement is architecture-dependent and that GPs outperform trained nets across dataset sizes -- an in-camp datapoint that the finite-width objection does not automatically favor the ensemble.

findings.location: ## N1 - Confound Taxonomy: Prior-Art Overlap and the Offline-MBO Residual
findings.issue: The research query explicitly listed Balduzzi et al. ('Re-evaluating Evaluation', NeurIPS 2018) among the six reality-check papers to check for N1, but the draft never mentions it. It was fetched and grepped (vault note present) and correctly found not to touch N1's shape -- but a novelty audit whose deliverable is 'exact queries run / prior-art checked' should record that a query-named paper was checked and ruled out, so the reader knows the full N1 list was addressed rather than silently dropped.
findings.evidence: Vault note re-evaluating-evaluation-neurips-2018-arxiv180602643 (Balduzzi et al.): 'Proposes Nash averaging... addresses evaluation-SUITE redundancy bias, not unreported implementation confounds; contains zero occurrences of confound/reproduce/baseline/tuning and does not touch N1's shape.' Query file lists Balduzzi explicitly in the N1 paper set; grep of the draft returns no 'Balduzzi' or 'Nash averaging' hit.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-clause parenthetical in N1 noting that Balduzzi et al.'s 'Re-evaluating Evaluation' was checked and ruled out as an N1 anchor because it addresses benchmark-suite redundancy (Nash averaging), not unreported implementation confounds -- closing the query's named-paper list without inflating the section.

findings.location: ## Executive summary (lines 3-7), ## Candidate Contributions (strategic recommendation, ~line 116), and ## AAAI-27 Venue Fit (~line 138)
findings.issue: Content dilution: the core strategic recommendation ('lead with D, present A as D's quantitative core, hold C back until the bidirectional manipulation is run') is stated three times in near-identical form, and the executive summary's second and third paragraphs pre-narrate the candidate recommendation and the three rejecting citations that later sections develop in full. At 61.7KB / ~9,000 words the report sits above the 45-55KB top-performer band and is drifting toward the 65-70KB bottom band; the repetition is the main driver.
findings.evidence: Exec summary line 5: 'do not build the paper on the dramatic reversal... nor on the surrogate-smoothness mechanism... Build it on the named, controlled, offline-MBO-specific confound set whose removal strengthens the effect.' Candidate section line 116: 'The strategic recommendation: lead with D, present A as D's quantitative core (with the optimizer null flagged as provisional), and hold C back until the manipulation is run.' Venue-fit line 138: 'File D under the benchmarking keyword, keep A as its quantitative core in the same submission... do not summon the Bayesian-learning pool until the bidirectional manipulation exists.' The same L/R/W-is-most-dangerous and Shahriari-reversal-killer points also recur across exec summary, N-sections, rejecting-citations, and venue fit.
findings.recommendation: Tighten the executive summary to a single paragraph that states the verdict distribution and the one-line D-recommendation, and let the candidate and venue-fit sections carry the developed argument. Keep the 'lead with D' recommendation in the candidate section only; in the venue-fit section replace the repeated recommendation with the keyword-mapping mechanics alone. This should recover several KB without losing any argument.

findings.issue: The executive summary and the candidate-section strategic recommendation (the report's de facto conclusion) restate the same D/A/C sequencing thesis with high phrase overlap, inflating length without adding value.
findings.evidence: Both passages assert the identical action set: build on the confound taxonomy (D), fold in the repaired measurement (A) as its quantitative core with the optimizer null flagged provisional, and defer the mechanism (C) until the bidirectional manipulation is run. The wording differs only cosmetically.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the two: keep the exec summary as the verdict-level thesis and reshape the candidate-section closer to emphasize forward-looking, strategic content already latent in the draft (the scoop risk from the IGNITE/ROOT lineage accelerating toward this territory, and the concrete next experiment C requires) rather than re-stating the sequencing recommendation verbatim.
